A_general.open_code_note: No Taskrabbit-owned MCP code was found in the prepared repository set. A community stdio wrapper exists at https://github.com/markswendsen-code/mcp-taskrabbit; it is not evidence for the hosted endpoint and was not treated as its implementation.
A_general.mcp_protocol_version: 2025-11-25 reported by Manufact; its report says legacy negotiation also succeeded

B_access_pricing.mcp_access_cost_details: No official MCP-specific price or access plan was found. An anonymous endpoint scan by Manufact reported tools/list results; this does not establish official pricing or availability terms.
B_access_pricing.linked_software_cost: Taskrabbit does not publish a fixed booking price in the cited fee page; clients pay the Tasker rate plus a Taskrabbit Service Fee, and applicable taxes may also apply.
B_access_pricing.pricing_model_details: Taskrabbit says its Service Fee is a percentage of the hourly Tasker rate and applies per hour worked; other taxes may apply by task location. MCP-specific charges, quotas, and per-call costs were not found.
B_access_pricing.other_access_restrictions: The observed tools use US postal codes and an en-US locale in their schemas. No official role, allowlist, regional MCP, or admin-enablement requirements were found.

D_server_side_logic.additional_logic: 1. Manufact reports behavior hints: check_service_availability and list_supported_services are read-only, idempotent, non-destructive, open-world; generate_deep_link is non-read-only, non-idempotent, non-destructive, not open-world. No official annotations source was found. 2. No server-enforced confirmation parameter or approval mechanism was documented. The generate_deep_link description says it creates a job draft and must follow the availability check; it does not state a confirmation requirement. 3. Authorization metadata URLs all returned 404. In contrast, Manufact reports an anonymous endpoint scan and Composio describes NO_AUTH; OAuth claims elsewhere conflict. Inherited user permissions, admin controls, allowlists, redirects, expiry, and revocation were not documented. 4. No read-only endpoint, tool filters, query-free mode, environment separation, or regional MCP variants were found. 5. Schemas solicit service details and location, including address and coordinates for link generation. No MCP-specific masking, PII exclusion, or scope boundaries were documented. 6. No MCP rate limits, quotas, bulk caps, time caps, truncation, or per-call costs were found. 7. Published third-party schemas include a five-digit postal-code pattern and alternative location requirements; no evidence of server-side coercion, unknown-argument behavior, or parameter overrides was found. 8. Taskrabbit MCP logging and telemetry were not documented. Composio describes its own logs and audit trail for its proxy service; that is not evidence of Taskrabbit server behavior. 9. No feedback, rating, report, or survey tool was in the three-tool list. The observed descriptions include a booking link flow but no upsell message. 10. No server-provided skills or initialize instructions were found. Tool descriptions include behavioral guidance; server-side enforcement of those instructions is unknown. 11. No evidence that prior agent behavior changes later outputs, tools, resources, or prompts. 12. No hierarchical or proxied Taskrabbit server structure was evidenced for this endpoint. A community stdio wrapper exists but is not the hosted server. 13. No raw API request, SQL, script execution, or general escape-hatch tool appears in the observed tool list.

E_aggregated.action_count_comment: No Taskrabbit-owned tool reference or public MCP code was found. Anthropic's Claude connector directory lists 3 exact tool names and labels the connector "Anthropic verified"; under the required source hierarchy, this directory remains third-party evidence. Manufact's endpoint report supplies schemas and annotations for those 3 tools. APIs.io and Composio also report 3 tools. mcp.so says no tools were detected in its fetch while naming the hosted endpoint; Switchy describes zero documented tools. No catalogue-only extra tool was evidenced. Full list is in actions.json.

actions.description: Checks local service availability, pricing, and scoping questions.
actions.parameters: service: string (required); city: string (required with state, alternative to postalCode); state: string (required with city); postalCode: string (5-digit US postal code; alternative to city+state)

actions.description: Creates a Taskrabbit job draft and returns a booking-flow deep link.
actions.parameters: categoryId: string (required); locale: string (required; enum 1: en-US); questionnaire: array (required; items require question and answer, optional param); location: object (required; address, postal_code, lat, lng all required)

actions.description: Lists Taskrabbit services available at a location.
actions.parameters: city: string (required with state, alternative to postalCode); state: string (required with city); postalCode: string (5-digit US postal code; alternative to city+state)

E_aggregated.token_method: No public implementation or initialize instructions were available. Manufact publishes tool metadata, but no official verbatim tool definitions plus initialize context were found to calculate the requested context count.
E_aggregated.human_can_agent_cannot: The MCP exposes service discovery, availability/pricing/scoping, and a job-draft booking link. It does not expose tools to select or book a Tasker, chat, pay, cancel, reschedule, or manage an existing task. Taskrabbit's consumer materials describe choosing Taskers, booking, payments, and cancellation/rescheduling; the difference is based on the observed three-tool list and public product documentation, not an explicit vendor statement of MCP exclusions.

F_documentation.implementation_hints_not_enforced: The observed tool descriptions guide the agent to provide either city plus state or a postal code, render topTaskers as visual cards, and call generate_deep_link after check_service_availability. No evidence shows these instructions are enforced by server logic.
F_documentation.governance_promises: No MCP-specific privacy, retention, data-use, logging, or governance promise was found. Taskrabbit's general privacy policy says booking information includes task, time, date, and location, and describes general platform data use; it does not specifically address MCP requests.
F_documentation.promises_to_user: Anthropic's directory labels the connector "Anthropic verified" and names Taskrabbit as the maker. The connector description says it provides location-based availability/pricing and booking links.
F_documentation.comparison_with_server_logic: The described availability and booking-link workflow is consistent with the three observed tool names and schemas. The verified badge and connector claims are directory-level statements; no Taskrabbit MCP documentation or code was available to check additional implementation promises.

contradictions: The provided OAuth metadata responses returned 404, and the supplied endpoint response included no WWW-Authenticate challenge; the Composio catalogue calls the connection NO_AUTH, while mcp.so describes OAuth sign-in. The endpoint evidence does not establish OAuth authorization.
mcp.so reports that its fetch detected no tools, while Anthropic's Claude directory, Manufact's endpoint report, APIs.io, and Composio each identify three tools.

Switchy says zero tools are documented and speculates about future/basic task operations; the Claude directory and other catalogues list three current tools. The speculative Switchy descriptions were not used as evidence for actions.
observations_for_research: The observed tool list includes two lookup tools and a draft/deep-link creation tool, with the latter described as dependent on a prior availability check.
The check_service_availability description contains a presentation instruction about rendering taskers as visual cards, alongside parameter guidance.
notes: Inspected links.json, links_check.txt, all prepared pages and scripts, and the code directory; it contained no official repository. Searches found no Taskrabbit-owned MCP documentation or tool reference. The linked Google Docs documentation URL exposed by Claude's directory was inaccessible to the browser. The Claude directory marks the connector Anthropic verified but is still third-party under this study's source rules. Unofficial community stdio repository: https://github.com/markswendsen-code/mcp-taskrabbit. Other catalogues contain unsupported or inconsistent auth/tool claims; these were not treated as authoritative.
